extracted.intended_audience: predoctoral applicants and reviewers for the NIH F99/K00 fellowship (career-development reviewers and selection committees)
extracted.subtask_description: Writing the 'Applicant's Background and Goals for Fellowship Training' and associated training plan for an NIH F99/K00 (predoctoral-to-postdoctoral) career development award, detailing prior experience, specific training goals, mentor roles, activities, timeline, percent effort, and specific aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of commitment to research population and topic
rubrics_metrics.description: Conveys a clear, sustained commitment to working with a defined vulnerable population and research area (e.g., "I decided to commit my research to this vulnerable group").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain why the population/topic matters, ground motivation in prior exposure/experience, and link commitment to future career trajectory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation of prior research experience and productivity
rubrics_metrics.description: Summarize past hands-on research, roles (e.g., co-investigator), outputs (manuscripts under review/preparation), awards, and presentations (e.g., IMTOP study, APHA Nobuo Maeda International Research Award, conference presentations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use concrete examples of data collection, analysis, supervision of students, manuscripts and awards to demonstrate preparedness for the proposed training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicit, numbered training goals and objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide specific training goals (e.g., "Training Goal 1: increase knowledge in prevention, intervention, and policy pertaining to cognitive decline", "Training Goal 2: gain skills in analyzing high-frequency digital biomarkers...", "Training Goal 3: learn to design, implement, and evaluate community-based interventions").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State goals clearly and tie each to concrete activities, mentors, and expected competency gains during F99 and K00 phases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detailed mentorship plan with named mentors and roles
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify co-sponsors/mentors (e.g., Dr. Iris Chi, Dr. Shinyi Wu, Dr. Hiroko Dodge, Dr. Lawrence Palinkas), specify how each mentor will contribute (directed reading, liaison to cores, qualitative methods training, implementation science consultation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe regular consultations, mentor responsibilities, access to cores/resources, and how mentors will facilitate training and career transition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Planned coursework and formal trainings
rubrics_metrics.description: List specific courses/training (e.g., GERO-566 Cognitive Decline course, ICPSR summer training, UCSF Study Designs for Intervention Research in Real-World Settings, NINDS Clinical Trial Methodology Course, self-directed R programming course).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include course names, timing (F99 vs K00), and how coursework will address gaps in knowledge/skills.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hands-on, immersive research and field experiences
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan to participate in real-world fieldwork and shadowing (e.g., observe I-CONECT field work, enrollment, setup, and trial monitoring; conduct focus groups; co-investigator roles in community studies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe specific field tasks, observation/shadowing plans, and expected learning outcomes (recruitment, enrollment, randomization, intervention delivery).

rubrics_metrics.name: Skills development in quantitative methods and data analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Acquire advanced statistical and data skills (e.g., structural equation modeling, longitudinal data modeling, multi-level modeling, Bayesian inference, R programming) to analyze longitudinal and high-frequency datasets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide training sources (courses, summer institutes), planned datasets for practice (NHATS, HRS) and link skills to planned analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training in neuroimaging and digital biomarker methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan hands-on training at specialized cores (e.g., OADC Neuroimaging core) and training in collecting/using digital biomarkers (wearable devices, in-home sensors).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how neuroimaging and digital biomarkers will be incorporated into research questions and how training will expand measurable outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of mixed-methods design and qualitative methods training
rubrics_metrics.description: Justify mixed-methods approaches as providing a holistic perspective; plan qualitative activities (focus groups, semi-structured interviews), purposeful sampling, and qualitative analysis (thematic/content analysis).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify qualitative mentors (e.g., Palinkas), describe development of interview guides, sampling plans, and how qualitative data will complement quantitative analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to and use of large, longitudinal secondary datasets
rubrics_metrics.description: Leverage existing datasets (e.g., NHATS, HRS, Health and Retirement Study) for longitudinal analyses and to prepare for high-frequency digital biomarker work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe planned waves/variables to be analyzed, how prior experience with these datasets supports feasibility, and how secondary data complement primary pilot data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pilot data collection to establish feasibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Collect pilot and formative data (e.g., focus groups, pilot studies like IMTOP pilot, ImPAHC) to inform intervention design and demonstrate feasibility prior to larger trials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain sample sizes, languages, data types (surveys, interviews), and how pilot results will feed into intervention refinement and manuscripts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intervention design, implementation, and evaluation training
rubrics_metrics.description: Learn to design, implement, and evaluate community-based interventions using real-world trial methods and implementation science perspectives (observe non-pharmacological trials, consult on implementation evaluation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include participation in trial methodology courses and consultation with implementation science experts to develop practical trial and evaluation skills.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear percent-effort allocation and realistic timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a year-by-year breakdown of percent effort across activities (research, mentoring, teaching, coursework, grant writing, conferences) for F99 and K00 phases (e.g., F99-Year1: 75% research, 10% coursework, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use explicit percentages and a calendar/timeline to show feasibility of training and protected research time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration of mentors, resources, and institutional cores
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate how mentors will connect the trainee to institutional resources (USC ADRC, OADC, neuroimaging cores) and external collaborations to broaden training opportunities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe mechanisms (liaison roles, meetings, core access) by which mentors facilitate training and resource use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissemination, networking, and scholarly engagement plan
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan for presenting results and building professional networks (submit abstracts to GSA, APHA, SSWR, AAIC; join special interest groups; attend investigator meetings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify conference targets, frequency, and how networking will support career development and collaborations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant-writing and funding strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Commit to continuous applications to NIH/other funders, participate in peer-support writing groups, attend Design Studio and Advanced Grant Writing courses, and budget time for grant preparation (5-10% effort).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State intended funding targets, timing of submissions (K00 phase emphasis), and formal supports for grant development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Teaching and mentoring as career-preparation activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Include concrete teaching (co-teach doctoral-level statistics) and mentoring responsibilities (5% effort) as preparation for faculty roles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe courses to be taught, mentoring plans for students, and how these experiences build evidence for future faculty hires.

rubrics_metrics.name: Career milestones and long-term trajectory
rubrics_metrics.description: Articulate measurable short-term and long-term career milestones (graduate with distinction, obtain another career development award within four years, secure tenure-track assistant professorship, achieve tenure within nine years).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide time-bound milestones that link training outcomes to career objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsible conduct and professional development activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Commit to training in responsible conduct of research and professional development activities (seminars, Design Studio, advanced grant writing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List planned RCR seminars and other professional development activities and indicate how they fit into the training timeline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focused Specific Aims linking theory, hypotheses, and methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Present Specific Aims that articulate the conceptual framework (e.g., Ecological Theory of Aging), research questions (longitudinal effects of living environment on social isolation and cognitive health), and proposed methods (NHATS longitudinal data, focus groups, examine ICT interactions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tie aims to testable hypotheses, explain mechanistic rationale (e.g., social isolation mediating environment-cognition), and align aims with training goals and mentor expertise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-modal measurement strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan to combine multiple outcome measures and modalities (physical environment metrics, neighborhood cohesion, self-report social isolation, cognitive testing, amyloid/neuroimaging measures, digital biomarkers) to comprehensively assess study questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how each modality contributes uniquely, and describe training needed to collect and analyze each data type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community-engaged research and partnerships
rubrics_metrics.description: Engage community-based organizations for recruitment, intervention adaptation, and dissemination (regular visits to collaborators, co-design with target populations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show sustained community relationships, describe co-design approaches, and indicate how community input will shape intervention feasibility and dissemination.
